Public Works Utility Operations
DATE: March 24, 2026
FROM: Michael Mart, Public Works Utility Operations Director
ITEM: Washington Street Master Lift Station Sole Source Purchase
REQUEST:
Sole source purchase of three replacement impellers and suction cover kits from General
Repair Service for the Washington Street Master Lift Station in the amount of $57,435.00.
BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
Three impellers and suction covers at the Washington Street Master Lift Station need to be
replaced. The lift station was built in 2012 with three Gorman Rupp dry submersible pumps.
The Washington Street Master Lift Station is a critical lift station in the city’s Sanitary Sewer
Collection System as it pumps approximately 50% of Bismarck’s sanitary sewer flows. All three
impellers and suction covers show extreme wear and have exceeded their serviceable life. We
are requesting the replacement with Gorman Rupp parts due to compatibility and tolerance of fit
with the existing pumps.
A written quote for $57,435.00 from General Repair Service in Vadnais Heights, MN is
attached. General Repair Service is the only regional representative available in the Bismarck
area who sells Gorman Rupp pumps and parts.
RECOMMENDED CITY COMMISSION ACTION:
Approve sole source purchase of three replacement impellers and suction cover kits from
General Repair Service in Vadnais Heights, MN for the Washington Street Master Lift Station in
the amount of $57,435.00.

Michael Mart, Public Works Utility Operations Director, 701-355-1704, mmart@bismarcknd.gov

Public Works Utility Operations
DATE: September 9, 2025
FROM: Michael Mart, Public Works Utility Operations Director
ITEM: Wachter Master Lift Station Pump Repairs
REQUEST:
Replacement parts purchase for Flygt pumps located at the Wachter Master Lift Station from
Electric Pump.
BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
The four Flygt pumps at Wachter Master Lift Station have electronic components (MAS-701)
inside the junction heads to monitor pump health, stator winding temperature, leakage in the
stator housing, leakage in the motor junction box, leakage in the oil inspection chamber,
bearing temperature, pump current, pump speed, and 3-axis vibration. The MAS-701 failed in
one of the pumps. The direct replacement part is MAS-801 as the MAS-701 has been
discontinued by the manufacturer. We are requesting the replacement of the MAS-701 units on
all four Flygt pumps with MAS-801 due to compatibility and tolerance of fit. This ensures that
the monitoring systems for all four pumps are in proper working condition per the
manufacturer’s recommendation. A quote of $79,375.00 for the replacement of all four units
from Electric Pump, the regional authorized representative for Flygt Pumps, is attached.
RECOMMENDED CITY COMMISSION ACTION:
Approve replacement parts purchase for Flygt pumps located at the Watcher Master Lift Station
from Electric Pump.

attachments.name: AIR - Sole Source Purchase of Snow Blower
attachments.text:
Airport
DATE: August 12, 2025
FROM: Gregory Haug, Airport Director
ITEM: Sole Source Purchase of Snow Blower Pump System
REQUEST:
Sole source purchase of snow blower pump system from Abi-Schmidt MB.
BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
The airport has a MB-4 high-speed snow blower for clearing wind rows and snow ridges off of
airport pavement surfaces. The MB-4 unit was purchased in 2019. One fault that the unit has is
that when it is operating at a low speed the ribbon that feeds snow into the impeller also runs at
a slow speed. This is happening because the hydraulic pump that operates the ribbon is tied to
the chassis drive engine. So, when the unit is at a slow speed, the drive engine is at a low
RPM, resulting in the ribbon spinning at a low RPM. When the ribbon is operating at a low
RPM, it doesn’t feed snow properly into the impeller and does not break up large pieces of
snow which leads to plugs. Unplugging leads to machine downtime and extra work for the
maintenance personnel operating the equipment.
Recently, Airport staff reached out to Abi-Schmidt MB staff and found that they have an
auxiliary pump system that can be installed to correct the low ribbon RPM at low speeds issue.
The cost of the pump system is $10,051.99, which, per City policy, would require three quotes.
Only Abi-Schmidt MB supplies the pump system, making the purchase a sole source. The cost
to purchase would come out of the airport’s approved spending plan.
RECOMMENDED CITY COMMISSION ACTION:
Approve the sole source purchase of a snow blower pump system for $10,051.99.
STAFF CONTACT INFORMATION:
Gregory Haug, Airport Director, 701-355-1805, ghaug@bismarcknd.gov
Matthew Remynse, Assistant Airport Director, 701-355-1806, mremynse@bismarcknd.gov

A Goulds Pump, Model 16X18-26EC, a low lift pump at the Water Treatment Plant, experienced

attachments.text:
Airport
DATE: August 25, 2026
FROM: Gregory Haug, Airport Director
ITEM: Sole Source Request for FlyMyAirport
REQUEST:
Sole source purchase of FlyMyAirport Website Tool.
BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
FlyMyAirport is a company that provides a website booking tool for airport websites. The
purpose of the website booking tool is to enhance an airport’s website by providing a travel
booking tool on the homepage that is easily accessible to passengers. The booking tool will
provide passengers with information on the multiple flight options outside of Bismarck Airport.
For airport staff, the tool monitors passenger search and purchase activity, which Airport staff
can use to improve air service and marketing efforts.
While completing research on the website tool, Airport staff found that FlyMyAirport is the only
company that provides a website tool that can provide this type of data. Also, while researching
website tool, Airport staff spoke with other airports for reference. Other airports reported that the
tool performs well, has created a new source of data, has increased airport website traffic and
has led to slight upticks in passenger travel.
Airport staff completed the Sole Source Procurement checklist with the Fiscal and received
approval. The initial cost to complete the purchase is $28,000. The ongoing cost is $25,000 per
year. The cost of the tool is incorporated into the airport spending plan.
RECOMMENDED CITY COMMISSION ACTION:
1. Approve sole source purchase of FlyMyAirport
2. Authorize Airport and City Staff to execute a three year contract with FlyMyAirport.

Finance Department
DATE: March 10, 2026
FROM: Eric Lund, Acting Finance Director
ITEM: Sole Source Purchase with Eagleview Pictometry
REQUEST:
Soul source purchase of high resolution, measurable oblique and orthogonal imagery annually
for 2026, 2027 and 2028.
BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
The Assessing Division of the Finance Department is the primary user of the EagleView
Pictometry program of measurable oblique and orthogonal imagery as part of our property
review process. We are able to view the imagery directly from our CAMA software or through
an app. The program is also used by CenCom, Fire, PD, Planning, Building Inspections,
Engineering, Public Works, and is shared with the public through our online maps. Staff is
requesting permission for sole source purchase of the updated imagery as the software is
compatible with existing City-owned technology and does not have proprietary software
restrictions against sharing with the public. We have completed the contract review process and
the purchase is accommodated in the annual assessing budget.
RECOMMENDED CITY COMMISSION ACTION:
Approve sole source purchase of updated high resolution, measurable oblique and orthogonal
imagery annually for 2026, 2027, and 2028 with Eagleview Pictometry.

Administration Department
DATE: October 28, 2025
FROM: Jason Tomanek, City Administrator
ITEM: Sole Source Purchase
REQUEST:
Update on a sole source purchase of a 1926 Seagrave fire truck approved at the September
22, 2025, City Commission meeting executive session.
BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
In 1926 the City of Bismarck Fire Department received a 1926 Seagrave fire truck that was
built-to-order for the Bismarck Fire Department. The apparatus was part of the Fire Department
fleet until 1988 when a local resident purchased 1926 Seagrave fire truck from the City of
Bismarck surplus auction in 1988. The owner of the fire truck offered to sell the vehicle to the
City. At the September 22, 2025 City Commission meeting the commission met in executive
session to discuss negotiation strategy to purchase the 1926 fire truck and directed City
Administration to present an offer to the owner. The offer was accepted as-presented and within
the limits set by the commission.
RECOMMENDED CITY COMMISSION ACTION:
Receive the update on the sole source purchase of a 1926 Seagrave Fire Truck.

matters.title: Sole Source Purchase of Ditch Grading

attachments.name: AIR - Sole Source Purchase of Ditch Grading
attachments.text:
Airport
DATE: August 12, 2025
FROM: Gregory Haug, Airport Director
ITEM: Sole Source Purchase of Ditch Grading
REQUEST:
Sole source purchase of ditching grading from Northern Improvement Company, Inc.
BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
As part of the Wetland Phase 5/6 Project (Project), the small tri-angular area of Airport property
northeast of the Lincoln Road and Yegan Road intersection was designed and constructed to
handle storm water discharges from the new airport lift station.
Airport staff have found that the lift station discharges storm water at a rate which is resulting in
the water rising beyond the banks of the ditch constructed under the project, and it is pooling up
on the flat areas. To correct the issue, the ditch banks need to be steeper to channelize and
contain the storm water and force it to flow down the cable concrete as originally envisioned. To
obtain the steeper ditches, additional dirt would need to be brought in from off-site and grading
work would need to be completed. Enclosure #1. This work will be outside the scope of the
original project.
Right now, Northern Improvement Company, Inc (NIC) is under contract with the airport to
reconstruct a portion of Taxiway C North. As part of the project, NIC is removing dirt from the
construction area because it is no longer needed to meet the grades around the new taxiway
pavement. This dirt is being hauled off site and disposed of. The dirt could instead be used to
regrade the ditches as described above.
Based on this idea, Airport staff received a quote from NIC to haul the waste dirt from the TXY
C North project to the project area, complete the necessary dirt work and grading, and reseed
the area. The NIC quote is $52,683. Airport staff also received a quote from Weisz and Sons to
complete the necessary work, and it was $85,998. The large difference in cost is because NIC
is already onsite completing work and would be using excess dirt from another Airport project.
Weisz and Sons would have to purchase dirt and mobilize, adding to the cost. The quotes are
in Enclosure #2.
Airport staff is requesting to complete a sole source purchase from NIC for this work. A sole
source purchase would save the Airport approximately $35,000 based off these two quotes. If
the Airport had to bid the work, we would lose the opportunity to use our own waste dirt. If not
approved, Airport staff will have to create a new project that will require design and bidding at a
later date. This will add cost to the project and the Airport will lose the ability to leverage a
contractor already mobilized and working on site. The Airport would likely see even higher
prices next year.
RECOMMENDED CITY COMMISSION ACTION:
Approve the sole source purchase of ditch grading from Northern Improvement Company, Inc.
STAFF CONTACT INFORMATION:
Gregory Haug, Airport Director, 701-355-1805, ghaug@bismarcknd.gov
Matthew Remynse, Assistant Airport Director, 701-355-1806, mremynse@bismarcknd.gov
ATTACHMENTS:
